text:
julian-cs: FYI, enterprise customer reports GitHub OAuth failing when initiated from an embedded iframe. Root error: `state mismatch` and PKCE `code_verifier` looks truncated on callback. They're on a recent Dedicated build.

maria-support: Oof. Do we have the exact redirect URL they hit? full query string?

julian-cs: Asked them to paste it, they sent back this (redacted): `https://app.customer.com/_auth/callback?code=...&state=🧩abc123%F0%9F%98%8A&session=xyz` — but the server logs show `state=🧩abc` (trimmed) and `code_verifier` ends with `...QWx` instead of the expected `...QWxhc3M=`.

sam-eng: Possible causes: URL length limit on their proxy, or a charset/encoding issue (emoji -> multibyte) causing truncation. Also browsers strip URL fragments in iframes sometimes. Are they using `response_type=code` with PKCE?

julian-cs: Yes `response_type=code` + PKCE. They load the auth flow inside an iframe to keep users in-app.

ingrid-infra: If the IdP redirects back with a fragment (#) instead of query params, those can be lost when routed through certain reverse proxies or if the app expects query params. But their example shows query params.

eng-sso: Two things to check: 1) nginx/ingress proxy `large_client_header_buffers` and `client_header_buffer_size` can chop long query strings or headers. 2) Any URL rewriting layer (CDN, WAF) that might percent-decode then re-encode emojis incorrectly.

maria-support: I asked them to repro with a simple public page (no iframe) to confirm. They say non-iframe flow works fine.

sam-eng: That matches iframe-specific behavior. Many browsers restrict third-party cookies and change sameSite semantics inside iframes; some IdPs fallback to `postMessage` or add a fragment step. If their app tries to read `location.hash` vs `location.search`, that mismatch will bite.

julian-cs: Customer sent server access logs showing `GET /_auth/callback?code=...&state=%F0%9F%8A%95ab` (looks percent-encoded emoji) and our frontend logs show `state=�ab` (replacement char).

ingrid-infra: Could be our URL decode library treating invalid UTF-8 sequences as replacement chars. But the truncated `code_verifier` points at a different layer (proxy URL length/clipping).

eng-sso: Quick repro steps I'd ask them to try:
1) Repeat flow with devtools open, preserve log, and capture the redirect URL exactly as the browser receives it.
2) Bypass any CDN/WAF/proxy (point DNS to origin) to see if proxy is mutating.
3) Try top-level redirect (not in iframe).
4) If they must use iframe, consider using expiring server-side state cookie tied to session instead of embedding emoji in state.

maria-support: I posted a short checklist to customer and asked for the raw redirect header capture and proxy logs.

julian-cs: Customer replied with this nginx error snippet: `upstream sent too big header while reading response header from upstream` and their ingress ingress-nginx config shows default `proxy-buffer-size` values.

sam-eng: That error strongly suggests header/body size limits. When the redirect contains a long query with multibyte emoji, it can push header size over the limit and the proxy may truncate. Workaround: move state into a server-side session cookie (short-lifetime) or shorten state (avoid emojis).

eng-sso: For our side: we should confirm token endpoint accepts PKCE verifier lengths we expect and that our redirect validation tolerates percent-encoded state with unicode. But since non-iframe works, likely customer infra is the culprit.

maria-support: Customer asked if Redwood can accept POST callbacks instead of GET to avoid long query strings. Is that possible?

sam-eng: Our OAuth compliance flow follows standard GET redirect for authorization code. We can’t change IdP behaviour, but customer can implement their own intermediate endpoint that receives the GET and then POSTs the smaller payload to their app. Suggestion: a tiny redirect relay under their control.

eng-sso: I'll open an internal ticket to look into any weird decoding quirks on our side (ENG-SSO-456). But mark low priority since repro only fails in iframe + through their proxy.

ingrid-infra: Also reminded customer to check `large_client_header_buffers` and `proxy_buffer_size` on their nginx and their CDN's max URL length. Increasing buffer sizes fixed similar reports.

julian-cs: Customer updated: after bypassing CDN, flow worked in iframe once. So CDN was mutating the query. They will file with CDN vendor.

maria-support: Marking this thread as resolved for now; asked customer to reopen if vendor fix doesn't hold. Thanks everyone :tada:

deploy-bot: Note: Created ticket ENG-SSO-456 with summary `Investigate percent-decoding + emoji state handling in auth callback` and assigned to sam-eng.
